It sounds like magic, or even like a violation of the laws of physics, but it is a rigorously proven theorem in set theory and geometry.    ### The Statement  The paradox states that a solid ball in 3-dimensional space can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint pieces (specifically, 5 pieces), which can then be reassembled using only **rigid motions** (rotations and translations) to form **two** identical copies of the original ball.    Essentially, you take one apple, cut it into a few weird, non-measurable chunks, and snap those chunks together to create two apples of the exact same size as the original. You can even repeat this process to create four apples, then eight, and so on.
